condition_other: Tourette syndrome / tic disorder (bicuculline-induced tic-like movements)
readout_other: video-tracked tic-like movement counts; single-channel EEG spike counts; c-Fos immunostaining; H&E staining; locomotion (DeepLabCut)
direction_notes: M2 sonication reduced tic-like movements by 51% and EEG spikes by 87% versus sham in the 5-minute window starting 15 minutes after recovery; general locomotion did not differ.
safety_notes: Focal temperature change was below 1 degC during sonication (thermocouple in a Petri dish) and H&E staining showed no tissue damage in targeted regions.

timing.protocol_description: 250 kHz, 100 Hz PRF, 2% duty cycle. The sonication lasted 20 minutes in total, with an inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 10 s; duration of each train not stated.

source_quotes.n_subjects: We further analyzed EEG signals to investigate the correlation between neural activity and tic-like movements, as well as the neuromodulatory efects of ultrasound stimulation. Compared to the DMSO group, the SHAM group exhibited a significant increase in EEG spike activity, which was identified as waveforms with a negative deflection immediately followed by a sharp positive peak. This heightened neural activity of the SHAM group was particularly prominent within the delta frequency band (see Methods and Figs. 5, 6a). Over the 30-minute observation period, the STIM group exhibited a substantial decrease in EEG spiking activities relative to the SHAM group (Fig. 5). In addition, temporally aligned EEG recordings and behavioral video revealed the synchronization of the tic-like movements with the onset of EEG spikes, which suggested the relationship between tic manifestations and underlying neural activity. The absence of EEG spikes during general locomotion and grooming, along with the lack of characteristic waveforms in control mice, suggested that the EEG activity observed in bicuculline-injected mice reflected pathological neural signals rather than motion artifacts (Supplementary Videos. 2-4). Notably, the STIM group demonstrated an 87% reduction in EEG spike counts during the 5-minute interval starting at 15 minutes after recovery compared to the SHAM group, which was consistent with the behavioral findings (Fig. 6b, Welch’s t-test, $t ( 5 ) = 4 . 9 1$ SHAM: $n = 4$ , STIM: $n = 4 , \ ^ { * * } p = 0 . 0 0 5 1 < 0 . 0 1 )$ . These results demonstrated that ultrasound stimulation of the M2 region efectively reduced the occurrence of abnormal EEG waveforms characteristic of the tic model. Furthermore, the EEG features observed in this study exhibited the potential utility as pathological neural correlates of tic-related disorders.
